llm.summary: The skill is local and consent-oriented overall, but it needs Review because it gives a path from private learning notes to generated skills that can be installed or published despite promising writes stay only in .learnings.

dimensions.detail: Capturing lessons, reviewing records, exporting archives, and drafting skills all fit the self-improvement purpose, but installing generated skills into skills/ or publishing them to ClawHub materially expands the impact beyond local note-taking.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The artifacts repeatedly say all writes require confirmation and stay in .learnings, yet the skill-generation flow allows user-confirmed writes to skills/ and external publishing; some natural-language triggers are broad enough to be invoked casually.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The package contains markdown documentation and a license only, declares no required binaries or environment variables, and the supplied static scan and VirusTotal telemetry are clean.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Most reads and writes are scoped to project-local .learnings data with stated sanitization, but synthesis from accumulated records into installable operational instructions is higher impact than ordinary logging.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Persistent learning logs, exports, and draft skills are disclosed under .learnings, but the documented option to install generated skills or publish them conflicts with the hard safety rule that only .learnings is written.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with a skill that records project learning notes and can synthesize them into new skill drafts. Before using the skill-generation feature, review generated content closely, avoid installing generated skills directly into your active skills directory unless you understand their instructions, and do not publish exports or generated skills if the learning records may contain private project details.
llm.findings:
[SDI-1] expected: Skill drafts and exports are disclosed as v0.3.0 features and mostly remain under .learnings, so that part is purpose-aligned; the material concern is the later install/publish path.
[SDI-2] expected: Auto-generating skill drafts is explicitly advertised, but propagating learned content into future agent behavior is high impact and should require careful preview and confirmation.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The scanner's concern about contradictory containment is supported for the skills/ and publish path, not merely for .learnings/skill-drafts or exports that are still inside .learnings.
[SQP-1] expected: Conversational trigger phrases are part of the intended user experience, but broad phrases like '怎么改进' or '打个分' can unintentionally start analysis or state-changing workflows.
[staticScan] expected: The static scan reported no findings, which matches the absence of executable code, hooks, dependency installs, or declared credentials in the artifact.
[VirusTotal] expected: VirusTotal telemetry was clean across the supplied engines; this supports but does not determine the verdict.
